title: Concentration of a normalized local dualizing complex in the Cohen–Macaulay case
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with finite Krull dimension $d$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Assume $\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}A=d$, with depth as in [def-weil-pbc-depth]. Let $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m$. Let $K\in D(A)$ be a normalized algebraic dualizing complex, meaning that $K$ is isomorphic to a bounded complex of injective $A$-modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions], every $H^j(K)$ is finitely generated, the scalar-action map $A[0]\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,K)$ is an isomorphism, and $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\kappa[0],K)\cong\kappa[0]$ in $D(A)$. Here $R\operatorname{Hom}_A$ is [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site. Then, putting $W=H^{-d}(K)$, there is an isomorphism
$$K\cong W[d]$$
in $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with shift convention $(L[d])^j=L^{j+d}$. The module $W$ is nonzero and finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], has support all of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ (its localization at every prime is nonzero), and $\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}W=d$.

proof.text: Fix a bounded injective representative $J$ of $K$. The bounded-below injective-complex lemma makes $J$ K-injective. By the definition of derived Hom, $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(A[0],K)$ is represented by $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_A(A[0],J)=J$, where evaluation at $1$ gives the equality. The support of the finite self-module $A$ is all of $\operatorname{Spec}A$: its annihilator is zero, so the support-annihilator criterion applies. Its support dimension is therefore $d$. Apply the degree-bounds and depth-detection lemma to $M=A$. Its clause (1) gives $H^j(K)=0$ for $j<-d$ or $j>0$; its clause (2), using $\operatorname{depth}A=d$, gives $H^{-d}(K)\ne0$ and $H^{-t}(K)=0$ for $0\leq t<d$. Thus $H^j(K)=0$ for every $j\ne-d$.

Put $r=-d$ and $W=H^r(J)$. This module is nonzero by Step 1 and finite by the hypothesis on $K$. Define a complex $T$ with $T^j=J^j$ for $j<r$, $T^r=\ker(d_J^r)$, and $T^j=0$ for $j>r$. Inclusion $T\to J$ induces the identity on cohomology through degree $r$ and is an isomorphism on all other cohomology because those groups vanish by Step 1. The quotient map $T\to W[d]$, equal in degree $r$ to $\ker(d_J^r)\to\ker(d_J^r)/\operatorname{im}(d_J^{r-1})$ and zero elsewhere, induces the identity in degree $r$ and an isomorphism between zero groups elsewhere. Both maps are quasi-isomorphisms. Inverting them in the derived category gives $K\cong W[d]$.

source.place: Tag 0AWS, concentration implies shifted-module form; explicit good truncation.

proof.text: If $a\in A$ annihilates $W$, it annihilates every term of $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_A(W[d],J)$: for an $A$-linear map $f$ out of its only nonzero source term, $(af)(w)=f(aw)=0$. This complex computes $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,K)$ by Step 2 and the K-injectivity of $J$. Thus $a$ acts as zero on $H^0R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,K)$. The scalar-action isomorphism in the hypothesis identifies that module $A$-linearly with $A$, so $a=a\cdot1=0$. Hence $\operatorname{Ann}_A(W)=0$. The support-annihilator criterion, applicable since $W$ is finite, now gives $W_{\mathfrak p}\ne0$ at every prime $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Full-support clause of the item: elementary consequence of homothety after concentration (an alternative to 0AWE(1)).

proof.text: Set $C=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_A(W[0],J)$, representing $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(W[0],K)$. Degree $n$ of $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_A(W[d],J)$ is $\operatorname{Hom}_A(W,J^{n-d})$. Multiplication by $(-1)^{dn}$ identifies it with degree $n$ of $C[-d]$; it commutes with differentials because the differential on $C[-d]$ is $(-1)^d d_C$. Consequently $C[-d]$ represents $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,K)\cong A[0]$, and $C\cong A[d]$ in $D(A)$. Its cohomology is nonzero exactly in degree $-d$, since $A\ne0$. Apply clause (2) of the depth-detection lemma to the nonzero finite module $W$: the least $t\geq0$ with $H^{-t}(C)\ne0$ is $d$, hence $\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}W=d$.
